topic: google uses gmail photos for ad targeting
headline_marked: Google privacy update: [[Gmail and Photos data]] may now be used for ad targeting
headline: Google privacy update: Gmail and Photos data may now be used for ad targeting
summary: Google's updated privacy policy removes previous limitations on using content from Gmail, Drive, and Photos for ad personalization, especially when connected via Personal Intelligence.
details: Google has updated its privacy policy, removing a specific clause that stated "We don’t show you personalized ads based on your content from Drive, Gmail, or Photos." The new language is more ambiguous, opening the door for this data to be used in ad targeting.

This change appears linked to Google's "Personal Intelligence" feature, launched in early 2026. This opt-in service allows users to connect data from multiple apps to Google AI products, aiming to provide better AI answers through added context.

While the Gemini app itself doesn't currently feature ads, sponsored content may appear in AI Mode search tools. Google's updated policy suggests that data shared with these AI search tools via Personal Intelligence could now contribute to ad personalization.

Google states that ads will not be "based directly" on personal data from Gmail or Photos libraries, and sensitive information will not be used for ad tailoring. However, they acknowledge that ads will remain relevant to queries, context, and user interests.

A Google spokesperson clarified that this policy update does not alter how data is handled with advertising partners and that personal data is not being scanned or shared with third parties. The core issue is that data piped into AI search tools could influence the ads displayed.

The company views the interconnectedness of its services and the wealth of data as a key strength for its AI development. While some apps like Gmail still have protected status, more avenues exist for data to be utilized across Google's ecosystem, increasing privacy risks.

Google also uses AI interactions for model training, stating it filters user activity to exclude personal data from training sets, though success isn't guaranteed. Personal Intelligence is opt-in, but the company uses prompts that may lead users to enable it without fully understanding the implications.

To prevent personal data from being used in ad targeting through this method, users must ensure Personal Intelligence is turned off. This setting can be found within the Gemini app settings or deeper within the main Google account settings under Data & privacy > Personalization settings.
